summary: Re-review after the fixes for the two minors from the 5179b836 round; only project.yaml and DESIGN.md changed, and no part code. The bench screw is now an M4 x 20 socket head (ISO 4762, 7.0 mm head, 4.0 mm tall), which seats in the base's 7.6 mm x 4.3 mm counterbore; the alternative is a wood screw with a head of 7 mm or less. This shows in the BOM row, DESIGN step 0 and the requirements row. `stand` is now min_deg 15 (ENGINEERING s10) and passes at 37.1 deg. The rebuilt report.json is a full build at this fingerprint (147 s, no problems), and every other result is unchanged: arm_torque 0.55/4.7, bracket_fea 0.64/13, arm_fea 4.59/24, mass 198.3/250, power 0.417. Audit findings A-8, A-15, A-16 and A-17 remain resolved.

findings.issue: The catalog entry electronics.connectors.dc_jack_5521_screw has no weight_g (kerf warning). The jack sits on the desk, not on the rig, so it does not affect rig_mass or stand.
findings.fix: Add a sourced weight to the catalog entry when one is available.

findings.issue: Carried over: tab_z is still unconfirmed (26.5 to 30.2 across sources). At 30.2 the horn disc has about 0.3 mm to the edges of the 20.56 mm window. DESIGN.md says to measure it before printing.
findings.fix: Measure the tab height on the real servo and catalogue it. Optionally make the window about 1 mm taller.

findings.issue: Carried over: the adapter's DC cord gauge is assumed to be 22 AWG, not sourced. The result does not depend on it.
findings.fix: Cite the GST60A datasheet's cable specification, or measure the cord.

findings.issue: The servo tab pilot holes and the arm's horn holes are under the 1.5 d edge distance (88 % ring material), because the purchased parts' hole patterns force it. DESIGN.md 'Edge distance' records the deviation and the FEA margin covers it.
